mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (as indicated by consecutive monthly decreases) signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of declining FEDFUNDS are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month period) signals deteriorating labor market conditions and impending economic slowdown, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and decline in industrial production (measured as UNRATE > 5.0% and INDPRO < 100) signals a severe economic contraction, triggering a flight to safety that depresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (UNRATE>5.0 and INDPRO<100) occurs in 20+ instances over 5 years, but SPX returns are positive in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: During post-recession recovery phases (as indicated by sustained growth in retail sales), a positive momentum in retail sales (RSAFS) signals strengthening consumer demand and corporate revenue growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the post-recession recovery regime, RSAFS growth is not associated with positive 60-day returns (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (as indicated by consecutive monthly increases) signals improving residential construction activity and broader economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in periods of rising HOUST are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp acceleration in the consumer price index (exceeding 0.2 percentage points over a 1-month period) signals rising inflation pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher interest rates.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in less than 40% of triggered instances, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts and industrial production (measured as HOUST > 1350 and INDPRO > 102) signals robust economic activity across multiple sectors, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate strong corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The interaction condition (HOUST>1350 and INDPRO>102) occurs in 20+ instances over 5 years, but SPX returns are negative in more than 60% of those instances.

mechanism_narrative: During early-cycle expansion phases (as indicated by rising industrial production), a positive momentum in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strengthening manufacturing activity and economic growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In the early-cycle expansion regime, INDPRO growth is not associated with positive 60-day returns (Rank IC < 0.05 over 3-year windows).
